description: Stop this solet without tearing down its infrastructure. The bound self-deployment plugin executes the actual stop. Cloud profile binds this to aws_self_deployment_plugin, which assumes the self-deployment role and calls ECS UpdateService with DesiredCount=0 on the currently-active service (resolved via the same listener-rule + target-group + version-parsing chain that deploy_status uses); polls DescribeServices until runningCount=0 within a bounded ~5min window. macOS profile binds this to macos_self_deployment_plugin, which writes a single cross-color drain sentinel at ~/.ananta/runtime/<solet>.draining and spawns a detached watchdog subprocess that SIGTERMs the solet child shortly after the verb returns. The watchdog escalates to SIGKILL after a bounded window if SIGTERM is ignored. Distinct from aws_undertaker_plugin::teardown_solet, which DESTROYS infra (RDS, ALB, ACM, KMS, S3, ECS service definitions); stop_self leaves ALL of that in place so the operator can bring the solet back later by re-setting DesiredCount=1 (cloud) or running ./launch.py (macOS — which scrubs the drain sentinel from _cleanup_stale_runtime_files and re-spawns the solet). Idempotent: a stop_self called while the sentinel is already on disk (macOS) or DesiredCount is already 0 (cloud) returns StopSelfStatus.ALREADY_STOPPED without re-issuing the kill. The reason argument is required — a stop without an audit message is undisciplined operator action; the verb refuses to default it.
embedding_description: Stop this solet without destroying its infra (distinct from teardown_solet, which destroys infra). Cloud sibling sets ECS DesiredCount=0 on the active service; macOS sibling writes a drain sentinel + spawns a watchdog to SIGTERM the solet. Idempotent; re-invoke returns already_stopped. Required reason audit. Returns StopSelfResult: status, reason, duration_seconds, stopped_at, action_id.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: StopSelfResult frozen dataclass with attributes: status (StopSelfStatus value — 'success' once the kill is queued or confirmed, 'already_stopped' for idempotent re-invocations, 'failed' when the verb could not complete, 'dry_run' when dry_run=True returned the planned actions), reason (echoes the operator-supplied audit string), duration_seconds (wall-clock seconds the verb spent — sub-second on macOS where the watchdog runs out-of-process, minutes on cloud where DescribeServices polling waits for runningCount=0), stopped_at (ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of confirmed-stopped on cloud; on macOS this is the moment the watchdog was spawned, since the SIGTERM fires shortly after), backend_action_id (backend-specific audit id — macOS spawned watchdog pid as a string so the operator can ps to confirm; cloud ECS service ARN), dry_run (echoes the dry_run flag), message (human-readable status detail).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: When status='success', surface the backend_action_id (watchdog pid for macOS, service ARN for cloud) plus the stopped_at timestamp so the operator can confirm. When status='already_stopped', surface that the solet was already in the stopped state — re-invocation was a no-op. When status='failed', surface the message verbatim — cloud-side failures typically come from ECS API responses (service not found, RolePassRoleRequired, etc.); macOS-side failures come from filesystem errors writing the sentinel or watchdog spawn failures. When dry_run=True, the response describes what would happen — sentinel path, watchdog parameters, ECS UpdateService call shape — without having executed it.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Stop the live solet without destroying its infrastructure (distinct from teardown_solet).
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: self_deployment_service_unavailable: no plugin is bound to self_deployment_service. missing_args: stop_self requires a non-empty reason string per the operator-discipline contract. role_assume_failed (cloud): sts:AssumeRole on the self-deployment role failed; the role's trust policy may have drifted. ecs_service_not_found (cloud): the currently-active ECS service could not be resolved via the listener-rule chain — typically means deploy_status would also fail. update_service_failed (cloud): ECS UpdateService rejected the desiredCount change. running_count_timeout (cloud): UpdateService succeeded but DescribeServices polling did not see runningCount=0 within the bounded window — tasks may be hanging in PENDING; check ECS console. sentinel_write_failed (macOS): filesystem error writing the drain sentinel (permissions, full disk). watchdog_spawn_failed (macOS): subprocess.Popen for the detached watchdog failed — check the Python interpreter resolution.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: self_deployment_service_unavailable: fix service_bindings.json. missing_args: re-invoke with a non-empty reason. role_assume_failed: verify the address-book entry for aws_self_deployment_role + the role's trust policy. ecs_service_not_found: confirm the solet's ALB listener rule still routes to a live target group; if the solet has been torn down then stop_self is moot. update_service_failed / running_count_timeout: the operator can fall back to `aws ecs update-service --cluster <c> --service <s> --desired-count 0` directly; the cloud-side verb is a convenience wrapper. sentinel_write_failed / watchdog_spawn_failed (macOS): the operator can SIGTERM solet process directly via `kill <pid>`; the LaunchAgent will respawn (since the sentinel never got written) which is operator-undesired, so first run `touch ~/.ananta/runtime/<solet>.draining` to suppress respawn before SIGTERMing manually.
